purpose.statedScope: "This Subject Benchmark Statement is relevant to all kinds of undergraduate and taught postgraduate degrees in Music, including broad-ranging Music degrees, cognate degrees such as Sound Studies and Music Production, degrees that intersect closely with other fields, such as Music Therapy and Musical Theatre, and specialised degrees within Music such as Ethnomusicology and Music Performance." (D1, 1.10)

digest.definition: Music in higher education is a wide field of intellectual and creative activity that builds specialist and general skills and opens many careers inside and outside music
distinctiveFeatures: Music in higher education is a wide field of intellectual and creative activity that builds specialist and general skills and opens many careers inside and outside music
Degrees differ greatly in content, method and approach; some keep to one tradition while others are plural, reflecting cultural diversity

Its distinctive elements are practice, creative invention, sensory skill, collaboration and special literacies such as notation and programming, which need space, instruments, technology, collections and practitioner staff
It can be arts- or science-based and meets many other subjects, from the humanities and business to engineering, physics, psychology, medicine and education

Every programme draws on linked activities: reading musical texts, creative and re-creative practice, analysis and criticism, repertories and their contexts, the social value of music, teaching music, aesthetics and reception, theory and practice, and vocational skills
It is offered by universities and specialist conservatoires, each with its own mission, to learners who arrive by academic, vocational or self-taught routes
Graduates often work for themselves in portfolio careers across music, education, broadcasting, healthcare and the wider cultural sector

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: music study questions inherited canons and privilege, opens to global, decolonial, disability-centred and gender-focused perspectives, and tackles unequal access to instruments, tuition and admission (D1, 1.12 to 1.17)

courses plan for disabilities that bear on music study (strain injuries, hearing and sight, performance anxiety, neurodiversity) and make lessons, ensembles, studios, placements and online material reachable (D1, 1.18 to 1.22)
students weigh the environmental and social footprint of music-making, from instrument materials and touring to the global music economy, and music is framed against the UN goals (D1, 1.23 to 1.26)
enterprise is built into the curriculum through events, commissions, briefs, microbusinesses, placements and practitioner staff, preparing students for freelance portfolio careers (D1, 1.27 to 1.36)
generative AI is used in teaching and assessed projects as a creative collaborator, with guidance on rights, plagiarism, labour, environmental cost and bias (D1, 1.37 to 1.41; 4.8)

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Music degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.appliesTo: music courses and course teams
statements.about: the Equality Act duty towards disabled students
statements.paraphrase: Every music course carries a responsibility under the Equality Act 2010 to weigh the needs of disabled students and act ahead of time so they meet no discrimination, harassment or victimisation; the paragraph lists conditions that bear on music study and says teams make spaces and equipment reachable for all.

forPractitioner.text: Plan for disabled students before anyone asks: consider the conditions that matter in music (strain injuries, hearing and sight, performance anxiety, neurodiversity, long-term illness), admit flexibly and make sure every student can reach studios, rooms, performance spaces and equipment.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Music degree

statements.appliesTo: students at the point of graduating
statements.paraphrase: Courses back students on their way into professional life; by graduation students will have begun professional networks and a personal brand, met hard problems in testing settings and grown resilient.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course so that, by graduation, students will have begun a professional network and a personal brand, tackled complex problems under pressure and built resilience; transferable skills and preparation for working life sit behind this.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate, you will have started a professional network and your own personal brand, worked through hard problems in demanding situations and grown more resilient.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Music degree

statements.appliesTo: students on honours and integrated master's courses in music
statements.about: progression across levels towards the threshold
statements.paraphrase: On an honours degree (FHEQ 6; FQHEIS 10) or integrated master's (FHEQ 7; FQHEIS 11) a student will move up level by level under the institution's rules, each level adding knowledge, expertise and experience towards at least the threshold in subject and generic skills; much of this builds cumulatively.

forPractitioner.text: Map each level so that it adds knowledge, expertise and experience that lead towards at least the threshold standards at the end, for example longer and more complex performance or composition, or deeper critical and contextual work.

forBeneficiary.text: Each year of your course will build on the last, adding knowledge, skill and experience, so that by the end you reach at least the minimum standard for the degree; expect your work to grow longer, more complex or more searching as you go.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Music degree

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates with a second-class degree or higher
statements.paraphrase: A music graduate with at least a second-class degree is expected to be able and ready to take on postgraduate study in music or a related field, though each provider sets its own entry requirements.

forPractitioner.text: Treat a second-class honours result or better as the point at which graduates are expected to be ready for postgraduate study; note that postgraduate entry rules are each provider's own and may ask for particular skills or marks.

forBeneficiary.text: If you finish with a second-class degree or higher, you can expect to be ready for postgraduate study in music or a related subject, though each course sets its own entry rules.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Music degree

statements.appliesTo: undergraduates studying music in a joint or combined degree
statements.paraphrase: Students taking music within a joint or combined degree, including major and minor routes, will reach the core of the subject and generic skills set out here and gain others from their other subject.

forPractitioner.text: In a joint or combined degree, make sure the music part delivers the core subject-specific and generic skills, while the partner subject adds its own; look for interdisciplinary openings where the two meet.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study music alongside another subject, you will reach the core music and general skills, and pick up further skills from your other subject.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Music degree

statements.appliesTo: degree-awarding bodies and their partners
statements.about: monitoring, review and the student voice
statements.paraphrase: Degree-awarding bodies and their partners gather and study information and review courses on their own cycle; the student voice will be part of this, and they use external reference points, this statement among them, to check alignment with sector norms.

forPractitioner.text: Build the student voice into routine monitoring and periodic review, and use external reference points such as this statement to check that provision sits within sector norms.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider about review; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Music degree

statements.appliesTo: providers conducting periodic review
statements.paraphrase: External scrutiny is a core part of UK quality assurance; providers will bring in reviewers from other institutions, professional bodies or employers during periodic review to gain an outside view and confirm that threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: Include external reviewers, from other universities, professional bodies or employers, in periodic review to give an independent view on proposed changes and to confirm the threshold standards and the subject content.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Music degree

statements.appliesTo: external examiners
statements.paraphrase: External examiners must write a report every year and suggest changes to modules and assessments where they see a need.

forPractitioner.text: Expect an annual report from each external examiner, with recommendations on modules and assessment where needed; arrange live attendance or recordings of recitals and event-based assessment so they can judge.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on external examiners and the provider; not a standard for the student

statements.appliesTo: assessment and feedback practice in music courses
statements.paraphrase: Because assessment is central to learning and professional skill, students are to be told clearly how assessment works and how marks are reached; criteria tied to outcomes and curriculum let them read their mark and see how to improve.

forPractitioner.text: Tell students plainly how each assessment runs and how the mark is worked out, and publish criteria aligned to the learning outcomes and curriculum so they can place their mark and see how to do better next time.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to be told clearly how each assessment works and how your mark is worked out, with criteria that show you how to improve your next piece of work.

statements.appliesTo: students receiving feedback on creative and performance work
statements.paraphrase: Since creative and performance assessment can turn on personal artistic expression, students will typically be able to talk through and query their feedback and be given ways to read and act on it, a skill the creative industries need.

forPractitioner.text: Give students room to talk through and question feedback on creative and performance work, and teach them how to interpret and act on it, as preparation for the creative industries.

forBeneficiary.text: Because creative and performance work is personal, you will usually get the chance to talk through your feedback, ask what it means and learn how to use it, which is a skill you will need at work.

statements.appliesTo: higher education providers awarding honours degrees in music
statements.about: going beyond the threshold; Annex D
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do well above the minimum threshold; each provider decides what evidence shows such achievement and should consult Annex D of the national qualifications Frameworks, which describes the four main honours classes.

forPractitioner.text: When deciding what evidence shows achievement above the threshold, you should consult Annex D of the UK qualifications Frameworks, which describes the first, upper second, lower second and third classes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: addressed to the provider about how it sets evidence for degree classes

statements.appliesTo: providers developing competence standards
statements.about: competence standards and the Equality Act
statements.paraphrase: The threshold and typical standards are not universal competence standards; a provider that sets competence standards under the Equality Act 2010 in a programme specification may draw on the statement and any PSRB requirements and should follow the latest guidance from the Equality and Human Rights Commission.

forPractitioner.text: Do not treat the benchmark table as a list of competence standards; if you set competence standards in a programme specification, base them on this statement and any PSRB requirements and follow the Equality and Human Rights Commission's current guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: addressed to the provider about competence standards; not a standard for the student

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.about: a body of music and its materials
statements.paraphrase: Will at least know and understand a body of music, together with the materials, texts, discourses and concepts that go with it in their discipline.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show what they know and understand of a body of music and of the artefacts, texts, resources and ideas attached to it in their field.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you know and understand a body of music and the materials, texts and ideas that go with it in your area.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: engaging in depth with scholarship on musical materials
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also be able to explore, assess, use or contest the scholarship and research on musical materials in depth.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to go further and engage in depth with the scholarship and research on their musical materials, exploring, testing, applying or challenging it.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will be able to explore, weigh up, use or argue against the research and scholarship on the music you study, in depth.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show knowledge and understanding of the contexts of music, including how it relates to historical, philosophical, cultural, educational and social practice.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show knowledge of the contexts music sits in: history, philosophy, culture, education and society.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you understand the settings music belongs to, such as its history, culture, philosophy, education and social life.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: critical debates about music in its contexts
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also be aware of the critical debates that arise when music is set in wider contexts.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also know the critical arguments that arise when music is read within its wider contexts.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also know the critical arguments that come up when music is placed in its wider setting.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show knowledge and understanding of how music connects with other fields in the arts, humanities and the social and physical sciences, where relevant.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show how music links with other disciplines across the arts, humanities and the social and physical sciences, as suits their course.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show how music connects with other subjects, such as other arts, the humanities and the social or physical sciences.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: what interdisciplinary work means for creation and research
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also be aware of what an interdisciplinary approach to music implies for making, innovating and researching.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also see what working across disciplines means for creative work, innovation and research in music.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also see what working across subjects means for how music is made, renewed and researched.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.about: analysing musical materials and reporting findings
statements.paraphrase: Will at least be able to analyse and question musical materials and artefacts in their discipline and report what they find coherently.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can analyse and probe the musical materials and artefacts of their field and present the results in a coherent form.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to analyse and question musical materials in your area and explain what you find clearly.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: debate and uncertainty raised by analysis
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also be critically aware of the questions of debate or uncertainty that analysing musical materials raises.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also recognise, critically, where analysis of musical materials leaves matters open or contested.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also be critically aware of where analysing music leaves questions open or in dispute.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show an understanding of how artistic practice relates to the theory of music, as it applies to their area.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show how artistic practice and theoretical thinking in music relate, in the area they study.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show how making music and thinking about it in theory relate to each other in your area.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also critique the nature, relevance, purpose and effects of theoretical constructs in music.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also critique the theories and frameworks used in music: what they are, why they matter, what they do and what follows from them.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also be able to critique the theories used in music: what they are, what they are for and what they lead to.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show an understanding of how music and technology relate.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show how music and technology shape each other.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show how music and technology are connected.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also show deep awareness of current discussion in and about music technologies, shown through critical writing or research through practice.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also show in-depth awareness of present debate on music technologies, through critical writing or practice-as-research.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also show a deep awareness of current thinking about music technology, through critical work or research through practice.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least convey personal expression and imagination when making music, using suitable technical and interpretative means.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can bring personal expression and imagination to practical music-making through apt technique and interpretation.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to put your own expression and imagination into making music, using the right technique and interpretation.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically show an individual musical personality or voice, through advanced technique and deeper interpretative insight.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to show a distinct musical personality, with advanced technique and deeper interpretative insight.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will show a musical voice of your own, backed by advanced technique and deeper insight into interpretation.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least recognise and use the essential components of musical language suited to their discipline and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can recognise and use the core elements of musical language that their field and practice need.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to recognise and use the basic building blocks of musical language in your area.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: musical language across cultures and genres
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also question how musical language is used in different cultural or genre settings.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also examine how musical language works differently across cultures and genres.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also be able to question how musical language works in different cultures or genres.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least recognise and respond to how music is organised, as their discipline requires.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can recognise and respond to the organisation of music in the ways their field needs.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to recognise how music is put together and respond to it, as your area needs.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also internalise musical materials and rebuild them, as suits the discipline.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also absorb musical materials and reconstruct them, in the way their field calls for.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also be able to take music in so fully that you can rebuild it yourself.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least collaborate in making music, through ensembles, co-creation, improvisation or similar work.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can make music with others, whether in ensembles, joint creation, improvisation or comparable activity.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to make music with other people, in ensembles, by creating together, improvising or in similar ways.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also show leadership within a creative team.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also lead within a creative team.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also show that you can lead within a creative team.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least use music technologies as the discipline needs, from recording and production to composition, sound design, instrument making, live events or generative tools.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can work with the music technologies their field needs, such as recording, production, composition, sound design, instrument building, live events or generative tools.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to use the music technology your area needs, such as recording, production, sound design, live events or generative tools.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also use the technology with nuance, creative flair and professionalism, in a way that suits the style.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also handle technology with nuance, creative flair and professional polish, in keeping with the style.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also use technology with subtlety, flair and professional polish, in a way that suits the style of the music.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show independent research skills and the potential to keep developing artistically and creatively.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show research skills of their own and promise of continued artistic and creative growth.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you can research on your own and that you can keep growing as an artist.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: potential for creative leadership and innovation
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also show the potential to lead and innovate artistically and creatively.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also show promise as artistic and creative leaders and innovators.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also show that you have it in you to lead and break new ground creatively.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least work on their own and show self-motivation and critical awareness of themselves.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can work independently and shows drive and critical self-awareness.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to work on your own, keep yourself going and look critically at your own work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also produce strong work on their own that is rigorous, defensible, robust and imaginative.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also produce independent work of a high standard that is rigorous, defensible, robust and imaginative.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also produce strong work of your own that is careful, well argued, sturdy and imaginative.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least work with others in diverse teams on shared projects or activities.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can work with others in mixed teams on joint projects or activities.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to work with a mix of people in teams on shared projects.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also show advanced teamwork, negotiation, organisation and decision-making.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also show advanced skill in teamwork, negotiating, organising and making decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also show advanced skill in working in a team, negotiating, organising and deciding.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least plan and manage a schedule of work well when carrying out a project.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can organise and run a work schedule effectively while delivering a project.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to plan and keep to a schedule of work when you carry out a project.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also plan and manage projects with confidence and adaptability.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also plan and manage projects confidently and adapt when things change.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also plan and run projects with confidence and adjust when plans change.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.about: respect for professional and cultural contexts
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show awareness of, and respect for, different professional and cultural contexts.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show awareness of and respect for varied professional and cultural settings.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you know about, and respect, different professional and cultural settings.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: adapting to settings and voicing the value of music skills
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also adjust creatively to varied professional and cultural environments and explain the value of musical, intellectual and creative skills there.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also adapt creatively to different professional and cultural environments and make the case for musical, intellectual and creative skills within them.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also adapt creatively to different working and cultural settings and explain what musical and creative skills bring to them.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.about: presenting work to expert and general audiences
statements.paraphrase: Will at least present work accessibly, so that expert and non-expert audiences alike can follow it, in sound, speech or writing.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can present work in a form both specialists and non-specialists can follow, through sound, speech or writing.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to present your work so that both experts and people new to it can follow, in sound, speech or writing.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also show imaginative and persuasive presentation.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also present imaginatively and persuasively.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also present your work in imaginative and persuasive ways.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.about: awareness of technical and technological skills
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show awareness of the technological and technical skills that suit their work.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show awareness of the technical and technological skills their work calls for.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you know which technical and technological skills your work needs.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically show advanced knowledge of how technical and technological skills are applied in their area.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to show advanced knowledge of applying technical and technological skills in the area they study.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will show advanced knowledge of how to apply technical and technological skills in your area.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.about: legal and ethical frameworks in music
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show awareness of the legal and ethical frameworks that apply to music practice and procedure.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show awareness of the legal and ethical rules that govern music practice and procedure, such as rights and consent.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you know the legal and ethical rules that apply to working in music.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: ethical and political challenges and ethical practice
statements.paraphrase: Will typically identify ethical and political challenges in music and act to make sure practice is ethical.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to spot ethical and political challenges in music and take steps so that practice stays ethical.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will spot ethical and political problems in music and take action so that the work is done ethically.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.about: communicating ideas in a creative team
statements.paraphrase: Will at least communicate musical and creative ideas well to others in a creative team.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can get musical and creative ideas across to others in a creative team.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to get your musical and creative ideas across to others in a creative team.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also adjust language and terms when communicating with a range of stakeholders.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also adjust their language and terms for the different people they deal with.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also change your language and terms to suit the different people you work with.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show awareness of how music bears on wider concerns in society.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show awareness of how music connects with wider questions in society.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you understand how music connects with wider issues in society.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.about: music and global and societal challenges
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also identify ways music can help to address global and societal challenges.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also identify ways music can help meet global and social challenges.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also be able to name ways music can help with global and social challenges.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will at least show they can adapt and go on learning.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every student can show adaptability and the capacity to keep learning.

forBeneficiary.text: At the minimum for your honours degree, you will be able to show that you can adapt and keep learning.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in music at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will typically also show they can help shape the future of music.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to also show they can contribute to where music goes next.

forBeneficiary.text: Going beyond the minimum, as most students do, you will also show that you can help shape where music goes next.

statements.appliesTo: students completing a master's degree in music
statements.about: systematic, critical grasp of current and emerging trends
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show a systematic, comprehensive and critically aware grasp of current and emerging directions in music research or practice.

forPractitioner.text: Expect master's students to show a systematic and thorough understanding of current and emerging directions in music research or practice, with critical awareness.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your master's degree, you will be able to show a systematic, thorough and critical grasp of where music research or practice is now and where it is heading.

statements.appliesTo: students completing a master's degree in music
statements.about: evaluating research to apply knowledge originally
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to assess current research and advanced scholarship and use knowledge in original ways in a field of music study or practice.

forPractitioner.text: Expect master's students to evaluate current research and advanced scholarship and apply what they know with originality.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your master's degree, you will be able to judge current research and advanced scholarship and use what you know in original ways.

statements.appliesTo: students completing a master's degree in music
statements.about: method, self-direction and originality with complex problems
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to weigh suitable methodologies and show self-direction and originality in handling complex problems in practice or research.

forPractitioner.text: Expect master's students to choose and justify methods and to tackle complex problems with self-direction and originality.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your master's degree, you will be able to weigh up methods and tackle complex problems in practice or research on your own initiative and in original ways.

statements.appliesTo: students completing a master's degree in music
statements.about: new insight, communicated to specialists and others
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to generate new insight in their field and convey conclusions clearly to specialist and general audiences.

forPractitioner.text: Expect master's students to produce new insight in their field and communicate their conclusions clearly to both specialists and non-specialists.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your master's degree, you will be able to come up with new insight in your field and explain your conclusions clearly to experts and to people outside it.

statements.appliesTo: students completing a master's degree in music
statements.about: a major practice project or substantial research project
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to complete a major practice project or a substantial research project grounded in a thorough understanding of the discipline.

forPractitioner.text: Expect master's students to carry through a major practice-based project or a sizeable research project, grounded in thorough understanding of the discipline.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your master's degree, you will be able to complete a major practical project or a substantial piece of research, built on a thorough understanding of your field.
